title: Abolish stamp duty for owner-occupier homes under $1.1 million
summary: The Greens would abolish stamp duty for owner-occupiers buying homes worth less than $1.1 million and discount it for homes between $1.1 million and $1.6 million; investors would not be eligible. The party says this would be funded by its ultra-wealth tax on property investors and a levy on big banks.
sourceTitle: Make Housing Affordable | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will abolish stamp duty for homes worth less than $1.1 million, and discount stamp duty for homes between $1.1 million and $1.6 million. But only for owner occupiers, not investors.

title: Build 88,000 public homes with initial $4 billion commitment
summary: The Greens would build 88,000 new public homes across Melbourne and regional Victoria, which they say would more than double public housing stock, and maintain and upgrade existing public housing. They commit an initial $4 billion, with more invested over time, and oppose demolition of the 44 public housing towers.
sourceTitle: Make Housing Affordable | The Australian Greens
excerpt: We will make an initial commitment of $4 billion, starting immediately, towards building, maintaining and upgrading public housing, with more invested over time.

title: Two-year rent freeze, then cap rent rises at wage growth or CPI
summary: The Greens would freeze rents for two years, ban rent increases in the first two years of every new tenancy, then cap annual rises at wage growth (or inflation if lower), with increases tied to the property rather than the tenant. The party cites PBO modelling it commissioned estimating the median renter would save $15,590 by 2030.
sourceTitle: Rent Caps Now | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Our plan is to freeze rents for two years, to give wages the chance to catch up to rents, and ban rent increases in the first two years of every new tenancy.

title: $50 million independent rental regulator and landlord licensing
summary: The Greens would establish an independent rental regulator with a landlord licensing scheme (licences revocable for serious or repeated breaches), required rent-worthy certificates and energy efficiency disclosure, and independent inspections. They would invest $50 million to set it up.
sourceTitle: Rent Caps Now | The Australian Greens
excerpt: We will invest $50 million in establishing the regulator.

title: New tenancy protections, including right to stay when home is sold
summary: The Greens would let renters stay when their home is sold to another investor, guarantee a right of return after renovations, introduce a 3-year re-leasing ban after a notice to vacate for owner or family occupation, and prohibit continuous recording at inspections.
sourceTitle: Rent Caps Now | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Introduce a 3-year re-leasing ban after a notice to vacate due to the landlord or a family member moving in

title: Abolish street auctions and require upfront reserve prices
summary: The Greens would abolish street auctions, require reserve prices to be disclosed at the point of advertising, require agents and buyers' agents to charge a fixed fee rather than a percentage, and make sellers pay for building, pest and energy efficiency reports.
sourceTitle: Make Housing Affordable | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Every home will have a clear price with the reserve disclosed upfront at the point of advertising.

title: Mandatory 30% affordable housing in developments of 15+ dwellings
summary: The Greens would require at least 30% genuinely affordable housing in new private developments of 15 units or more, prohibit sale or lease of public housing land to private developers, and legislate a definition of 'affordable' as rent within 30% of the tenant's income.
sourceTitle: Make Housing Affordable | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Requiring a minimum of 30% genuinely affordable housing in new private developments of 15 units or more across the state

title: Legislate goal to end homelessness by 2036; right to housing in Charter
summary: The Greens would legislate a goal to end homelessness by 2036, add the right to housing to Victoria's Charter of Human Rights, and guarantee long-term funding for homelessness services and specialised housing for vulnerable cohorts.
sourceTitle: Make Housing Affordable | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Legislate a goal to end homelessness by 2036

title: Ultra-wealth land tax on investors with $5m+ residential portfolios
summary: The Greens would replace existing land tax for property investors owning more than $5 million in residential investment properties with a $100,000 base rate plus 5.3% on value above $5 million. The party says this would raise about $2 billion over four years, directed to stamp duty cuts.
costing: Party estimate: raises approximately $2 billion over four years (about half a billion a year)
sourceTitle: Make Housing Affordable | The Australian Greens
excerpt: It will increase the base rate for portfolios of $5 million and over to $100,000, and the rate for any amount above $5 million to 5.3%, and will replace existing land tax for these properties.

title: 0.1% quarterly levy on big banks' Victorian liabilities
summary: The Greens would impose a quarterly levy of 0.1% on Victoria's share of the liabilities of the big five banks (ANZ, CommBank, Westpac, NAB and Macquarie). The party says it would raise more than $3 billion a year.
costing: Party estimate: raises $3+ billion a year
sourceTitle: How we will pay for our plans | The Australian Greens
excerpt: We’ll put a quarterly levy of 0.1% on Victoria’s share of bank liabilities, starting immediately and raising an extra $3+ billion a year.

title: Raise online gambling, casino table and pokies taxes
summary: The Greens would raise the online gambling tax to 25% and stop that revenue going to racing, double the tax on casino table games, and raise pokies taxes to 75%. The party says this would raise more than $2 billion a year.
costing: Party estimate: more than $2 billion a year
sourceTitle: How we will pay for our plans | The Australian Greens
excerpt: We’ll immediately increase the tax on online gambling to 25% (like they have in the ACT) and stop the revenue from going to racing, double the tax on table games at the casino, and raise the taxes on pokies to 75%.

title: Double coal and gas royalties
summary: The Greens would double existing royalties on coal and gas and end subsidies and tax exemptions for fossil fuel projects. The party says doubling royalties would raise about $80 million a year.
costing: Party estimate: about $80 million extra a year
sourceTitle: How we will pay for our plans | The Australian Greens
excerpt: We’ll immediately double the existing royalties on coal and gas, raising about $80 million extra a year.

title: Raise windfall gains tax on rezoned land to 75%
summary: The Greens would increase the tax on property developers' windfall profits from land rezoning to 75%.
sourceTitle: How we will pay for our plans | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will immediately increase the tax on property developers' windfall profits when land is rezoned, to 75%.

title: Double and enforce vacant residential tax; extend to commercial property
summary: The Greens would raise the vacancy tax to 2%, 4% and 6% in the first, second and third years a home is empty, move from self-declaration to active enforcement, and apply a 3% site-value tax to metropolitan commercial properties empty for six months or more a year. The party says this would raise hundreds of millions a year.
sourceTitle: Rent Caps Now | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Double the vacancy tax, with investors paying 2% in the first year, 4% in the second year and 6% in the third year that a property is empty.

title: End build-to-rent land tax discount and absentee owner exemption
summary: The Greens would end the 50% land tax discount and absentee owner surcharge exemption available to build-to-rent developments.
sourceTitle: Make Housing Affordable | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will immediately end the BTR land tax and absentee owner exemptions and put money back into local communities for the things we need.

title: Trial 10 publicly owned supermarkets with $350m over four years
summary: The Greens would open 10 publicly owned supermarkets (five in metropolitan Melbourne, five in the regions) pricing essentials 30% below the major chains and stocking locally sourced food. The party says households would save an average of $82.20 a week on essentials.
costing: $350 million over four years (party figure, initial investment; also covers farm-gate pricing and price-gouging caps)
sourceTitle: Cheaper Groceries | Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: We’ll immediately invest $350m over the next four years as an initial investment in this nation-first trial and in giving farmers a fair deal and caps on supermarket price gouging.

title: Essential Services Commission to cap essential grocery prices
summary: The Greens would empower the Essential Services Commission to set maximum prices for key essential grocery items, reviewed monthly, and to set minimum farm-gate prices for farmers on essentials.
sourceTitle: Cheaper Groceries | Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Under our plan, the ESC would set maximum prices for key essential grocery items, which would be updated and reviewed monthly.

title: Greens Power Voucher for home energy upgrades and EVs ($500m)
summary: The Greens would offer vouchers of up to $1,500 for owner-occupiers and $3,000 for renters for solar, batteries, insulation, electric hot water, reverse-cycle air conditioning, induction cooktops and draught-proofing, up to $3,000 off electric cars, e-bikes and two-way chargers, and free energy assessments for renters.
sourceTitle: Sustainable Homes | Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: It is worth up to $1500 for owner-occupiers, and $3000 for renters, to make it easier to persuade their landlords to improve the property.

title: Plug-in balcony solar regulations by 2027
summary: The Greens would fast-track regulations to allow plug-in balcony solar systems in 2027, give renters the right to install them, and require new apartment buildings to be balcony-solar ready.
sourceTitle: Sustainable Homes | Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will fast-track regulations to make Plug-in Balcony Solar Systems a reality in 2027

title: Make public transport permanently free
summary: The Greens would make public transport free permanently across Victoria.
sourceTitle: Transport - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: And we will make public transport permanently free.

title: Trams and trains at least every 10 minutes, 7am–10pm
summary: The Greens would run trams at least every 10 minutes from 7am to 10pm, and trains at the same frequency across most of the network where infrastructure allows, and would duplicate the Upfield line to enable 10-minute services.
sourceTitle: Transport - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Run trains at least every 10 minutes from 7am-10pm across most of the network, where infrastructure allows

title: $270 million to reform Melbourne buses and upgrade regional buses
summary: The Greens would spend $270 million to progressively reform suburban Melbourne buses into a fast, frequent grid and upgrade local bus services in regional Victoria.
sourceTitle: Transport - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Spend $270 million to progressively reform buses into a fast, frequent grid, across suburban Melbourne, and upgrade local buses in regional Victoria

title: $245 million for more frequent regional trains and coaches
summary: The Greens would invest $245 million in frequency improvements for regional train and coach services.
sourceTitle: Transport - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Run regional trains and coaches more often, by investing $245 million in frequency improvements.

title: $225 million initial investment in accessible tram stops
summary: The Greens would make an initial $225 million investment in building accessible (level-access) tram stops.
sourceTitle: Transport - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: will start with a $225 million initial investment in building accessible tram stops.

title: $80 million a year for safe bike routes
summary: The Greens would dedicate $80 million a year to building a network of safe bike routes (the Strategic Cycling Corridors) across Melbourne and regional centres, and support 30 km/h limits in residential streets, around schools and in high-pedestrian areas.
sourceTitle: Transport - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: will dedicate $80 million a year to building a network of safe bike routes across Melbourne and regional centres

title: Double registration fees for vehicles with bonnets over 120cm
summary: The Greens would double registration fees for vehicles with bonnet heights over 120cm, which they describe as posing greater danger to pedestrians and cyclists.
sourceTitle: Transport - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will immediately double registration fees for vehicles with bonnets over 120cm

title: Infrastructure Victoria to produce 30-year Integrated Transport Plan
summary: The Greens would give Infrastructure Victoria the power and resources to create an Integrated Transport Plan with a 30-year investment pipeline, and require the government to publicly justify major projects that deviate from it.
sourceTitle: Transport - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will give independent advisory body Infrastructure Victoria the power and resources to create a detailed Integrated Transport Plan, with a 30-year investment pipeline.

title: $3 billion Local Transport and Initiative Fund
summary: The Greens would create a $3 billion seed fund within the general government sector to fund local transport projects and other local initiatives.
sourceTitle: Transport - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will create a $3 billion Local Transport and Initiative Fund, to fund our local transport projects, as well as other local initiatives.

title: Return road maintenance to public hands
summary: The Greens would bring road maintenance and VicRoads back into public hands, starting with an urgent inquiry to set a roadmap, and reinvest any savings in road repairs.
sourceTitle: Transport - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will bring road maintenance back into public hands.

title: $3 billion over 10 years to make public dental free for all
summary: The Greens would invest $3 billion over 10 years to expand free public dental care to all Victorians (excluding cosmetic and orthodontic), including facilities, workforce, removing out-of-pocket costs, vouchers for private care while capacity is built, and prevention. The party says it would be funded by taxing gambling corporations.
sourceTitle: Make Dental Free - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: We will invest $3 billion over 10 years to expand free dental care to everyone across Victoria

title: Open 20 publicly owned free dental clinics
summary: As part of its dental plan, the Greens would open 20 publicly owned clinics providing free dental care in regional Victoria and inner and outer Melbourne, with more over time.
sourceTitle: Make Dental Free - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: We will open 20 clinics in a range of locations including regional Victoria and inner and outer Melbourne, while opening more over time.

title: $200 million to retain VicHealth
summary: The Greens would commit $200 million to keep VicHealth, Victoria's health promotion agency, and increase prevention and health promotion funding elsewhere in the health budget.
sourceTitle: Health - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will commit $200 million to save VicHealth

title: Lift community health spending to 3% of health budgets
summary: The Greens would set community health spending at 3% of existing health and health infrastructure budgets, reprioritised from admitted and non-admitted services, to fund publicly funded GPs and allied health.
sourceTitle: Health - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will make spending on community health services 3% of the existing health and health infrastructure budgets

title: Ban junk food, alcohol and gambling ads on state-owned assets
summary: The Greens would ban advertising of junk food, alcohol and gambling on all state-owned billboards, buses and trams.
sourceTitle: Health - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will ban advertising of junk food, alcohol and gambling on all state-owned billboards, buses and trams.

title: Fund public schools at Victoria's full SRS share by 2028
summary: The Greens would bring forward full funding of Victoria's share (75%) of the Schooling Resource Standard for public schools to 2028, rather than 2031.
sourceTitle: Education - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: While Labor is promising to pay Victoria's share by 2031 (75% of the Schooling Resource Standard), the Greens will bring this forward to 2028

title: $1 billion for school Disability Inclusion funding
summary: The Greens would invest $1 billion in disability support in schools, reversing cuts to Disability Inclusion funding, and hold an urgent review of ongoing funding needs.
sourceTitle: Education - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will reverse Labor’s cuts to Disability Inclusion funding, by investing $1 billion in disability support now.

title: Independent school building authority to allocate upgrades by need
summary: The Greens would establish an independent school building authority so school building and maintenance decisions are based on need.
sourceTitle: Education - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will establish an independent school building authority, so decisions about school building are based on need instead of marginal seats

title: Cap private school public funding at 100% of SRS; free solar for schools
summary: The Greens would cap public funding for private schools at 100% of the Schooling Resource Standard and fund solar panels for government schools through non-repayable grants.
sourceTitle: Education - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: by capping their funding at 100% of the funding the Gonski review said was needed to meet students’ educational needs.

title: Cap university vice-chancellor salaries and review university acts
summary: The Greens would cap vice-chancellor salaries and review Victoria's eight public university acts to embed student and staff voices in university governance.
sourceTitle: Free University & TAFE | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will cap vice-chancellor salaries, so more university funding can go towards providing quality education.

title: Extra $2 billion for the SEC and a public energy retailer
summary: The Greens would provide an immediate extra $2 billion to the State Electricity Commission for publicly owned renewables, including solar on schools, public housing and government buildings, and establish a publicly owned energy retailer within the SEC.
sourceTitle: End Coal and Gas | Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Undertake a massive build of publicly owned renewable energy, with an immediate extra $2 billion for the State Electricity Commission.

title: Ban offshore oil and gas drilling and stop Viva gas import terminal
summary: The Greens would ban oil and gas drilling in Victoria's oceans, including near the 12 Apostles, stop Viva Energy's gas import terminal, and block all new fossil fuel projects in Victoria.
sourceTitle: End Coal and Gas | Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Ban oil and gas drilling in our oceans, including stopping Labor’s drilling near the 12 Apostles, and stop Viva’s gas import terminal.

title: Close Yallourn in 2028 and switch off Loy Yang A units early
summary: The Greens would ensure Yallourn's four coal units close as planned in 2028 and invest in renewables so individual Loy Yang A units can be switched off before its scheduled 2035 closure.
sourceTitle: End Coal and Gas | Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Ensure Yallourn’s four coal-burning units close as planned in 2028, and invest in renewables to enable individual units at Loy Yang A to be switched off earlier than planned, before its scheduled closure in 2035.

title: $1 billion climate adaptation fund; polluters to fund disaster clean-up
summary: The Greens would establish a $1 billion climate adaptation and mitigation seed fund for communities affected by climate disasters, make big polluters fund disaster clean-up, and legislate to let people affected by climate disasters sue coal and gas companies.
sourceTitle: End Coal and Gas | Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Establish a $1 billion climate adaptation and mitigation seed fund, for communities impacted by climate disasters(within the general government sector).

title: Moratorium on new AI data centres
summary: The Greens would impose an immediate moratorium on new AI data centres, require data centres to run on 100% newly built renewable energy without gas or diesel backup, and make operators compensate residents affected by existing facilities.
sourceTitle: AI Data Centres - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens are calling for an immediate moratorium on all new AI data centres

title: $2 billion nature fund for environment protection and restoration
summary: The Greens would create a $2 billion seed fund to restore environment funding and fund First Nations-led protection and restoration of Country, including invasive species control, threatened species recovery and purchase of land for the Western Grassland Reserve. Feral deer would be reclassified as a pest.
sourceTitle: Protect & Restore Nature - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will create a $2 billion seed fund to reverse Labor’s cuts to nature protection and fund First Nations-led work protecting and restoring Country.

title: New Central Highlands and East Gippsland parks; close logging loopholes
summary: The Greens would create permanent legal protection and new national parks and reserves for forests in the Central Highlands and East Gippsland, repeal laws allowing native logging to return on public land, ban native forest logging on private land, and ban Victorian mills processing native timber.
sourceTitle: Protect & Restore Nature - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Create permanent legal protections, and new national parks and reserves, to protect forests in the Central Highlands and East Gippsland, with Traditional Owners' rights and management front and centre.

title: Ban duck shooting and overhaul wildlife laws
summary: The Greens would ban duck shooting, overhaul Victoria's wildlife laws and permit system, and redirect funding that promotes recreational hunting to species and habitat protection.
sourceTitle: Protect & Restore Nature - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Overhaul our wildlife laws and fix the permit system that allows massive numbers of native animals to be killed

title: Make the Birrarung Yarra swimmable by 2036 ($70m)
summary: The Greens would legislate a target to make the Birrarung Yarra safe to swim in by 2036, with $70 million initial investment in restoring the river and creeks including the Merri and Moonee Ponds Creeks.
sourceTitle: Protect & Restore Nature - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: We will also legislate a target to make the Birrarung Yarra safe to swim in by 2036, with $70 million in initial investment to restore the river and its surrounding ecosystems

title: 20c container refund, more single-use plastic bans, incinerator moratorium
summary: The Greens would increase the container deposit refund from 10 to 20 cents and extend it to wine and spirit bottles, ban more single-use plastics such as bread tags, soy sauce fish, coffee cups and produce bags, and seek a moratorium on waste incineration projects.
sourceTitle: Waste and Recycling - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will ban more single-use plastics, like bread tags, soy sauce fish, coffee cups, produce bags and fruit and veg stickers.

title: $1 billion Office of Community Safety and Crime Prevention
summary: The Greens would invest $1 billion in community safety, establishing an Office of Community Safety and Crime Prevention to coordinate prevention programs, including statewide 24/7 crisis outreach teams of health, mental health and social workers.
sourceTitle: Community Safety - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will invest $1 billion into community safety, investing in what works.

title: Raise age of criminal responsibility to 14; repeal 2025 bail changes
summary: The Greens would raise the age of criminal responsibility to 14 and repeal the 2025 bail changes and life sentences for children.
sourceTitle: First Nations and Treaty - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: We will also repeal Labor’s 2025 bail changes and life sentences for kids.

title: Legalise and regulate cannabis
summary: The Greens propose a legally regulated and taxed cannabis industry, with licensed dispensaries and cannabis cafes and home growing of up to six plants, ending criminalisation of people who use cannabis. They also propose decriminalising personal drug use and possession and expanding pill testing.
sourceTitle: Drug Harm Reduction - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens propose a legally regulated, taxed, and quality-controlled industry for cannabis that will improve consumer safety, undercut organised crime and focus on harm reduction.

title: Ban corporate political donations
summary: The Greens would ban big corporate donations to politicians, candidates and parties, including from gambling, property and fossil fuel interests, and ban property developer donations in local government elections.
sourceTitle: Integrity - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will get money out of politics by banning big corporate donations to politicians, candidates and political parties.

title: Truth in political advertising laws
summary: The Greens would introduce South Australian-style truth in political advertising laws.
sourceTitle: Integrity - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will introduce South Australian-style Truth in Political Advertising Laws.

title: Public lobbyist register and post-politics lobbying ban
summary: The Greens would legislate a public register of lobbyists with sanctions for breaches, and laws preventing MPs and ministers moving straight into lobbying roles after leaving office.
sourceTitle: Integrity - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will legislate a public register of lobbyists, with real sanctions for lobbyists who do the wrong thing

title: Cap election campaign spending and local government donations
summary: The Greens would cap election campaign spending, as in NSW and the ACT, and introduce donation caps for local government elections.
sourceTitle: Integrity - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will cap campaign spending, like they have in New South Wales and the ACT.

title: Legislate to prevent privatisation of public services
summary: The Greens would introduce legislation to stop public services being sold off, and hold an inquiry into returning road maintenance and electricity to public ownership.
sourceTitle: Integrity - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: Introduce legislation to stop public services being sold off.

title: $200 million to replace ageing fire trucks
summary: The Greens would invest $200 million to replace ageing fire trucks and legislate an annual rolling replacement program.
sourceTitle: Rural & Regional Victoria - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will invest $200 million now, to replace ageing trucks, as well as legislating an annual rolling replacement program

title: $100 million to restart sick pay scheme for casual workers
summary: The Greens would restart the casual sick pay scheme, giving casual workers five days of paid sick or carer's leave a year, with $100 million.
sourceTitle: Workers Rights | Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will commit $100 million to restart the scheme.

title: Implement all Yoorrook Justice Commission recommendations ($50m initial)
summary: The Greens would implement all recommendations of the Yoorrook Justice Commission, starting with an initial $50 million, and oppose any repeal of Victoria's Treaty legislation.
sourceTitle: First Nations and Treaty - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will implement all, starting with an initial investment of $50 million.

title: Ban greyhound racing and jumps racing; end racing funding
summary: The Greens would ban greyhound racing with a welfare plan for dogs and a transition plan for workers, ban jumps racing, and cancel government financial support for horse racing.
sourceTitle: Protect Animals - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will immediately ban greyhound racing, with a welfare plan for the future of greyhounds currently in the industry, and a just plan for trainers and other workers to transition to other employment.

title: Abolish council rate capping
summary: The Greens would abolish rate capping so councils can set rates according to local needs.
sourceTitle: Local Government - Platform | The Australian Greens
excerpt: The Greens will abolish rate capping so councils can work together with their communities to set rates according to local needs.
